title: Absolute Difference
description: Given two integers a and b, return the absolute difference between them.
hints: Subtracting can give a negative number.
Python has a built-in that removes the sign.
reference_solution:
def solve(a, b):
    return abs(a - b)

title: Even or Odd
description: Given an integer n, return the string "even" if n is even, otherwise return "odd".
hints: What does n % 2 give for even numbers?
reference_solution:
def solve(n):
    return 'even' if n % 2 == 0 else 'odd'

title: Maximum of Three
description: Given three integers a, b and c, return the largest one.
hints: You can compare with if/elif, or use a built-in.
reference_solution:
def solve(a, b, c):
    return max(a, b, c)

title: Count Vowels
description: Given a string s, return the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in it. Count uppercase and lowercase letters.
hints: Convert to lowercase first so you only check five letters.
reference_solution:
def solve(s):
    return sum(1 for c in s.lower() if c in 'aeiou')

title: Factorial
description: Given a non-negative integer n, return n! (the product of all integers from 1 to n). By definition, 0! = 1.
hints: Multiply it by every number from 2 up to n.

title: Second Largest Distinct
description: Given a list of integers, return the second largest distinct value. If there is no second distinct value, return -1.

examples.explanation: Distinct values sorted: 1, 2, 3, 4. The second largest is 3.

hints: Duplicates should count once. Which data structure removes them?
If fewer than 2 distinct values remain, return -1.

title: Remove Duplicates Keep Order
description: Given a list of integers, return a new list with duplicates removed, keeping the first occurrence of each value in its original order.

examples.explanation: Later repeats of 1 and 2 are dropped.

hints: A plain set() loses the order.
Track values you have already seen while building a new list.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings a and b, return True if b is an anagram of a (same letters with the same counts, ignoring case), otherwise False.
hints: Two words are anagrams if their sorted letters are equal.
reference_solution:
def solve(a, b):
    return sorted(a.lower()) == sorted(b.lower())

title: First Unique Character
description: Given a string s, return the index of the first character that appears exactly once. If there is none, return -1.

examples.explanation: 'v' is the first character that appears only once.

hints: First count how many times each character appears.
Then scan the string again and return the first index whose count is 1.

title: Fibonacci Number
description: The Fibonacci sequence starts 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ... where each number is the sum of the previous two. Given n, return the n-th Fibonacci number (F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1).
hints: A loop that keeps the last two values avoids repeated work.
